name: INOrganization
title: India Organization Profile
description: Country-layer profile for Organization under Indian jurisdiction. Authored by this project, NOT an official NRCES/ABDM-published profile — the identifier-system URIs below are project-chosen placeholders; swap in the real NRCES canonical URLs if/when integrating with India's official ABDM FHIR Implementation Guide. Requires a GSTIN and a PAN tax-registration identifier on every Organization, each format-checked, plus an optional Health Facility Registry (HFR) identifier (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission) for healthcare-facility Organizations specifically. Each of the three requires `use` to be populated, restricted to 'official' or 'temp' — these are registry identifiers, not the kind of thing 'usual'/'secondary'/'old' naturally describes, but a temporary/provisional registration is a real, legitimate case. Extensions are deliberately disallowed (Organization.extension narrowed to max=0 below) since none are defined yet — arbitrary custom data can't be smuggled in under this profile until a specific extension is explicitly added and modeled as a real slice.
_comment_element_order: IMPORTANT, empirically verified, two separate ordering quirks in this validator version (org.hl7.fhir.validation 6.5.18) — not documented spec behavior, not something to rely on if the validator is ever upgraded, but both required for this file to work correctly today: (1) within each slice, every OTHER child sub-element (e.g. .use) must be listed BEFORE the discriminator's own target sub-element (.system here, since slicing.discriminator.path='system') — with .system first and .use second, the discriminator failed to resolve for every slice ('Could not match discriminator (system) ... does not have fixed value, binding or existence assertions'); .use first, .system second fixed it. (2) the plain Organization.extension max=0 constraint below must be listed BEFORE the Organization.identifier slicing block, not after — with it listed last (after all the identifier elements), the gstin/pan/hfr-id required-slice checks silently stopped being enforced entirely (a minimal payload with zero identifiers passed validation with no errors at all, confirmed empirically) — moving the exact same max=0 element to the front of this array restored correct enforcement with no other change. Neither failure mode is visible at /profiles registration time (always 200 OK); both only surface as wrong /validate behavior — (1) as a confusing discriminator error, (2) as required checks silently not firing. This key is not a real StructureDefinition field — it's a note for whoever edits this file next.

element.comment: No custom extensions are defined for this profile yet, so max is narrowed to 0 — none are permitted at all, deliberately. Base R4 leaves Organization.extension wide open to any URL with any content; this profile locks that down rather than inheriting it, so arbitrary/ungoverned extension data can't ride along under India's profile. The day a specific extension actually needs to be supported, replace this with a real slicing declaration (discriminator on .url, per FHIR's standard extension-slicing convention) plus that one named slice — a slicing intro with zero slice members is NOT equivalent to max=0 on this validator version: empirically confirmed it fails snapshot generation entirely ('has no snapshot') for a slicing block with no slice members, regardless of open/closed, so max=0 is used here instead, not as a style preference. Must stay BEFORE the Organization.identifier block below — see _comment_element_order above.

slicing.description: Slices Organization.identifier by system to separately track India-specific registry identifiers (GSTIN, PAN, HFR ID) alongside any other identifiers an organization may carry — 'open' so unrelated identifiers (DUNS, internal references, etc.) are still allowed.

constraint.human: GSTIN value must match the standard 15-character GSTIN format (2-digit state code + 10-character PAN + entity code + check digit + checksum).
GSTIN identifier's use must be 'official' or 'temp'.
PAN value must match the standard 10-character PAN format (5 letters + 4 digits + 1 letter).
PAN identifier's use must be 'official' or 'temp'.

element.comment: 0..1 at this generic country layer since not every Organization using this profile is itself a healthcare facility. A tenant-layer (organization-scope) profile for an actual hospital/clinic/lab/pharmacy would tighten this to 1..1 — narrowing an already-allowed 0..1 down to 1..1 is a legal profile-of-a-profile per the narrowing rule (see docs/structure-definitions/05-cardinality-and-multiplicity.md).

constraint.human: HFR ID identifier's use must be 'official' or 'temp'.
